_readme: The domain map. ONE source of truth for which product lives on which domain.
HOW TO USE IT: buy a domain, paste it into that product's `domain` field, run
`node tools/domains.mjs`, commit. The script regenerates the host rewrites in
vercel.json, rewrites the canonical and og:url tags on that product's pages,
and builds a per-host robots.txt and sitemap. Point the domain's DNS at the
host and it is live.
Leave `domain` empty for anything not bought yet. Empty products are skipped
and keep serving from the apex exactly as they do today. The script is a
total function of this file: clearing a domain puts everything back on the
apex, and running it twice changes nothing the second time.
WHY A GENERATOR AND NOT 40 HAND-EDITS: every product page hardcodes
https://tbsol.net/... in its canonical and og:url. Move a product to its own
domain without updating those and Google keeps indexing the tbsol.net copy —
the new domain never ranks and the two compete with each other. That is the
one mistake that makes this whole exercise backfire, and it is exactly the
kind of thing that rots when done by hand across dozens of files.
ONE CODEBASE, MANY DOMAINS. Nothing here forks the repo or the hosting
project. Every domain is served by the same deploy and the same files; only
what sits at `/` changes per host. A fix to booking or rewards lands on all
of them at once — which is the opposite of what happens if each product
becomes its own copy of the site.
_sitemap_exclude_why: /shop/ with no ?c= says "no shop selected". The useful URLs are /shop/?c=<slug>, one per shop, and those belong in each shop's own Google listing — not in TB's sitemap.

products.name: Loop
products.status: LIVE — bought 2026-08-11. www is the primary host in Vercel (the apex 308s to it), so the domain is recorded in its www form and canonicals name it that way.
products._wall_off_why: Nick: the barber domain should be barber content only. These are TB's other public products/pages — on thebarberloop.com they bounce to the Loop home. NOT walled: /rewards/ /kit/ /booking/ /ambassadors/ /crm/ /center/ /affiliate/ (barber-facing tools linked from the landing page and prebuild), and /privacy/ /terms/ /sms-terms/ (legal must stay reachable on every host).

products.name: TB University
products.buyer: people who want to start a marketing business — a different audience to Loop
products.status: WAIT. Buy when the course is actually for sale.

products.name: TB Studio
products.buyer: small businesses wanting free content — a lead magnet, not a paid product
products.status: WAIT. Only worth a domain if it gets pushed as a standalone free tool.

products.name: TB Command
products.buyer: local businesses buying the whole bundle
products.status: WAIT. Overlaps Loop and has no customers.

_clients._why: Client brands. They own their own domains — Nick does not buy these, and their canonical tags must never be pointed at tbsol.net or their own SEO gets absorbed into his.

depends_on_tbsol: /capture/?c=hubsandbabydoll  — their inquiry form. Served from tbsol.net.
?c=hubby and ?c=babydoll resolve to the same client slug.
hubsandbabydoll._risk: Their lead form lives on Nick's hosting. When tbsol.net went dark on 2026-08-09/10, their inquiries had nowhere to land. Leads submitted during an outage are not queued — they are lost. Worth either moving the form onto their own domain or accepting that their lead flow is only as reliable as this account's billing.

_stays_on_the_apex._why: Not products with their own buyer. A domain each costs money every year and splits what little SEO exists across sites nobody searches for.
_stays_on_the_apex./booking/: Chair. The Sites tab already lists it as parked — it duplicates the booking inside Loop.
_stays_on_the_apex./crm/: Part of Command, not a separate thing to sell.
_stays_on_the_apex./learn/: Local SEO content for TB Solutions itself. It should stay on the apex where it already ranks.
_stays_on_the_apex./privacy/: One legal entity, one privacy policy. Reachable from every domain at the apex path.
_stays_on_the_apex./sms-terms/: Same — and Twilio's campaign registration points at this exact URL. Moving it breaks that registration.
